# Donelon Wild School of Dance (DW Dance)

> A children's dance school in Stretford, Greater Manchester, teaching ballet,
> tap and modern to ages 3–18 across Stretford, Flixton, Urmston and Davyhulme.
> Founded in 2016 by Bethany Donelon and Sally Wild. Classes run from complete
> beginner to student grade, with optional NATD examinations. The first class
> is always free.

## Key facts

- **Name:** Donelon Wild School of Dance (short form: DW Dance)
- **Founded:** 2016, by Bethany Donelon and Sally Wild
- **Principal:** Miss Bethany Donelon
- **Location:** Based in Stretford, Greater Manchester, England
- **Venues:** Stretford, Flixton, Urmston, Davyhulme (all in Trafford)
- **Ages taught:** 3 to 18
- **Dance styles:** Ballet, Tap, Modern
- **Levels:** Complete beginner through to student grade
- **Examinations:** NATD (National Association of Teachers of Dancing) — optional
- **Class groups:** Pre-School (3–5), Junior (6–9), Intermediate (10–13), Senior (14–18)
- **Trial:** First class free, no obligation
- **Performances:** A full theatre show every other year; watch weeks and
  demonstrations every year, including the years between shows
- **Email:** miss.bethany@dwdance.co.uk
- **Telephone:** 07910 603360 or 07778 323321
- **Dancewear store:** https://ddw.mydancestore.co.uk/

## Common questions this site answers

- What age can a child start dancing? Pre-School classes take children from
  age 3. Senior classes run to 18.
- Does a child need previous experience? No. Every age group accepts complete
  beginners, and children are placed by stage rather than school year.
- What should a child wear to a first class? Comfortable clothes and bare feet
  or socks. Uniform is only needed after enrolling.
- Are dance examinations compulsory? No. NATD exams are optional and children
  are entered only when their teacher judges them ready.
- Is there a sibling discount? Yes, from the second child onwards.
- Is the trial class really free? Yes, one free class with no obligation.
- Where are classes held? Stretford, Flixton, Urmston and Davyhulme, in Trafford,
  Greater Manchester.
